title: Underwriting Bulletin: FloodGuard Anti-Selection Load on Limit Increases after a Reported Claim
content:
Underwriting bulletin — FloodGuard Private Flood Policy.

A limit increase requested soon after a flood claim is reported carries an anti-selection load. An anti-selection load raises the additional premium for the limit increase by 25 percent when the most recent flood claim on the policy was reported no more than 90 days before the increase was requested; by 10 percent when it was reported more than 90 days but no more than 365 days before the request; and by nothing when no flood claim was reported within the 365 days before the request.

**Measure.** Calendar days from the date the most recent flood claim on the policy was reported (its first notice) to the date the increase was requested, as recorded on the limit-increase entry.

**Bands and their edges**

| Days from the most recent claim report to the request date | Anti-selection load |
|---|---|
| 0 to 90 | 25 percent |
| 91 to 365 | 10 percent |
| more than 365, or no flood claim ever reported on the policy | none |

- Reported 90 days before the request: 25 percent. Reported 91 days before: 10 percent.
- Reported 365 days before the request: 10 percent. Reported 366 days before: none.

**Hypothetical illustrations**

- An increase requested on 2025-08-01 on a policy whose most recent flood claim was reported on 2025-06-15 (47 days earlier) carries a load of 25 percent.
- The same request with the most recent claim reported on 2024-12-01 (243 days earlier) carries 10 percent.
- The same request with the most recent claim reported on 2024-05-01 (457 days earlier) carries no load.
